892.by: Andrew Beling (ajbeling), with AI agents (Claude Opus 5.5) and an independent AI review (Claude Opus 5.5)
892.supersedes: The block of 29 Oct 2026 (partly_read) had not seen any cipher; from the archive's descriptions it already noted the 19th-century decipherment of 8-3-12, the clear draft of 8-2-24 at 8-2-10 fol. 74 and the archive's citation of Austro-Turcica for all five. 'No decipherment' is in the lead's status field, not in that block. This block adds: all five items seen at reading size; three of them are Latin, not Italian as the lead says; 16th-century interlinear decipherments over the cipher lines of the originals of 8-2-22 and 8-3-10 (every cipher line on the images we viewed); the 19th-century decipherment of 9-1-2; a pencil gloss on 8-2-24; tests of the malvezzi1548 key brief on all five. With every cipher passage deciphered on record, the verdict becomes read.

Images not reproduced here.
seen.extent: 8-2-22 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 24 Mar 1550, Italian; original with four cipher passages of about 46 lines, deciphered between the lines on every page viewed; a duplicate in cipher without gloss; 8 images); 8-2-24 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Vienna, 25 Mar 1550, Latin, 26 cipher lines, 2 images; clear draft 8-2-10 fol. 74); 8-3-10 (Malvezzi to Ferdinand, Constantinople, 22 Apr 1550, Italian, about 50 cipher lines, deciphered between the lines on both pages viewed, 2 images); 8-3-12 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Brno, 28 Apr 1550, Latin, original 42 cipher lines and duplicate 29 lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 6 images); 9-1-2 (Ferdinand to Malvezzi, Augsburg, 3 Oct 1550, Latin, 3 cipher lines, plus a 19th-century decipherment, 3 images).
seen.cipher: Graphic-sign homophonic cipher of Malvezzi's alphabet (signs such as circle on a stem, hash, two bars, Greek letters, numerals for doubled letters, null words Cum, Porro, Spo, Dar; code words Ras, ki, ka, zus, zos). Decipherments on or with the leaves: 16th-century Italian glosses over the cipher lines of the originals of 8-2-22 and 8-3-10 (every line on the images viewed); 19th-century 'Entzifferung' sheets with 8-3-12 (images 5-6) and 9-1-2 (image 3); a modern pencil gloss over lines 1-3 of 8-2-24. Cipher of 8-3-12, 8-2-24, 9-1-2, 8-3-10 fol. 160r and two passages of 8-2-22 transcribed twice (the second blind) and decoded with the upstream malvezzi1548 key (lead892_test/, lead892_rest/).

prior_art.edition: Austro-Turcica 1541-1552, ed. Karl Nehring (Munich 1995), HathiTrust mdp.39015038445451, search only; no page seen. The archive's description of each item cites it: 8-2-22 pp. 415-418, 8-2-24 pp. 418-419, 8-3-10 pp. 433-434, 8-3-12 p. 437, 9-1-2 p. 513. HathiTrust full-text phrase searches (23 Nov 2026, logged in search_log_hathitrust.md, result pages not saved) support the citation: phrases from the decipherments of each item return this volume, e.g. 8-3-12 'quemadmodum a Rege suo sibi iussum', 9-1-2 'de successibus omnibus certiores facere pergas', 8-3-10 'ogniuno se lamenta', 8-2-22 'non se dechiara el tempo' (the Italian phrases from our own reading of the glosses); for 8-2-24 the hits may come from the draft of 17 March printed on pp. 410-415. Some phrases were not found.
prior_art.literature: In this repository: targets/malvezzi1548 (Daniel Bourdeau, the 1548 letter and the key brief from DECODE R367/R386, used here); targets/huyson1547 (Brice Dudout's K-C01, calibrated on Türkei I 7-3-20 and tested on 8-3-8; not used here and not on these items); lead 2682 (vetted read, 16 Nov 2026), the rest of Türkei I Kt. 8-9, which names 8-2-22, 8-2-24 and 8-3-10 as its overlap with this lead and records from the Hungaricana regests that the Malvezzi cipher pieces are deciphered and printed in Nehring. No open issue or pull request names lead 892, Malvezzi or Türkei (gh search, 23 Nov 2026).

892.key_check: Daniel Bourdeau's targets/malvezzi1548/KEY_BRIEF.md, unedited (SHA-256 66f98502...c7793fd, as upstream), with links from its word descriptions to the 1550 sign shapes made by us and frozen before decoding (some wrong; README). Decoded mechanically from blind transcriptions against the witness on record, pass marks in hashed plans, 200 shuffled keys: 8-3-12 0.924 (pass mark 0.85); 8-2-24 0.875 against its clear draft (0.85); 9-1-2 0.911 (0.85); Malvezzi's Italian 8-3-10 fol. 160r 0.783 and two passages of 8-2-22 0.739 against our reading of the interlinear glosses (0.80, missed). The key beats every shuffled key on all five (best 0.392-0.478; an independent re-run with 2,000: best 0.414-0.511). The 1550 copies also use a looped q, & and a star as nulls, and alpha for x, which the brief does not list.
892.duplicates: Catalogue 500 lists Türkei I 7-1-4, 7-2-18, 7-2-25, 7-3-39, 8-3-8, 8-3-11, 8-4-6, 9-1-8, none of these five; targets/huyson1547 used 7-3-20 and 8-3-8. Lead 2682 (read) covers the remainder of Türkei I Kt. 8-9 'beyond the ones in leads 891/892' and names 8-2-22, 8-2-24 and 8-3-10 only as the overlap to match against this lead: related, not a duplicate.

892.closed: Read at the time: the ciphered passages of Malvezzi's 8-2-22 and 8-3-10 are deciphered between the lines of the originals in a 16th-century hand; 8-3-12 and 9-1-2 have 19th-century decipherments filed with them; 8-2-24 has its clear draft at Türkei I 8-2-10 fol. 74. The archive cites Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 for each (pp. 415-418, 418-419, 433-434, 437, 513; no page seen, HathiTrust phrase hits support it). Lead 2682 (read) records the same for the rest of these boxes. The malvezzi1548 key brief with our sign links reads the Latin letters 8-3-12, 8-2-24 and 9-1-2 above the pass marks (lead892_test/, lead892_rest/).
